They are described as Dwarvish in build but more adapted for permanent life underground, with large eyes and little hair. *Year 419 - Skirmishes arise over control of the mines as the Orakur claim the settlers are stealing minerals from what they refer to as the "Great Underground". By Year 423 these small skirmishes had escalated into war, later to be called The Plague Wars. Dwarven settlers sign an accord absolving themselves from warring with Orakur because of a perceived kinship. Because of this accord, the Dwarven people abandon their claims and leave Thaermore; Thaermore forever becomes predominately occupied by the race of Men. *Year 425 - While mining for copper a settler named Sam of Thorabur discovers a massive gemstone that would become known as "The Crux of Ages". Because of the ongoing conflict with the Orukur the rough stone is hidden away in Bastion Spire, a stronghold which would later become the capitol of Thaermore. *Year 433 - The first governing body of Thaermore is formed. It was decreed that a lifetime Chancellor would be elected to represent the will of people. He is given the highest authority and has a council of twelve advisors, known as The Grand Scholars, serve with him. *435 - Chancellor Marr is elected as the first governor of Thaermore. Under his leadership, Thaermore establishes the Commonwealth Guard, which becomes the turning point in the war with the Orakur. *444 - The Orakur are suppressed and driven deep underground. Chancellor Marr declares victory in the war. The Orakur disappear completely and many assume the whole populous must have succumbed to disease or starvation. Dwarven Lords from outside Thaermore condemn Chancellor Marr for his unethical warfare tactics; relations between the race of Dwarves and Men are fractured. *471 - Chancellor Marr dies after 36 years of distinguished service. Chancellor Marr II, later known as "The Great One", superseded his father as Chancellor. This officially begins the golden age of expansion and prosperity for Thaermore. *509 - Chancellor Torrus I supersedes Chancellor Marr II. *537 - Chancellor Katerra I supersedes Chancellor Torrus I. *[There is an entry here that has been blackened out by ink] *590 - Goblin skirmishes arise in Crakamir. The Chancellor, unwilling to squander resources defending a wasteland, concedes Crakamir to the Goblins. Elsewhere in Thaermore, the Commonwealth Guard is successful in eliminating the Goblin threat. *627 - A devastating earthquake shakes the eastern province, tearing great rifts into the land. The Orakur, long believed to have been decimated, reappear from the great fissures. Surveyors who spot them claimed they appeared skittish and non-hostile. Elusive and rarely seen above ground, the reappearance of the Orakur is not considered a threat and they are all but forgotten. *The timeline ends here, although it looks like the following page may have been ripped from the book.

evidence.text: "Goblin Clans of Thaermore" *Goblins have always been a nuisance to the people of the eastern provinces. Like weeds and mosquitoes, it was a common acceptance that goblins were just here to annoy us, mucking around and causing trouble. Luckily the common goblin is just that- a nuisance that is easily scared away when confronted. Early settlers learned that just keeping a dog nearby or a lantern lit was usually enough to keep the Goblins from stealing chickens at night. *This changed in the late 5th century when Goblins began to organize themselves into clans. Suddenly there appeared Goblin war units capable of causing great harm to others. They stopped being a nuisance and became a danger. During the skirmishes of 590, the Commonwealth Guard experienced noted difficulty in suppressing Goblin raids in the southlands. After securing most of Thaermore, a large wall called the Southern Gate was built to keep the Goblins contained in Crakamir. Human settlers were evacuated from the desert lands. The Chancellor proclaimed it a victory for humans; the Goblins clans claimed it a victory for themselves. *Much was learned of the Goblin war clans at that time. The basic warrior, called the Goblin Hacker, uses a short sword or machete in a savage but effective attack. Goblin Archers have been witnessed to have impressive accuracy with short bows. And the Goblin Bombthug, a unit strapped with a keg of Bangdust, is fully prepared to sacrifice himself in the defense of the unit or a higher officer. Although most Goblins are not known to possess magickal abilities, there are reports of Goblin Shaman among the clan population. *The Goblin unit is loosely assembled and generally led by a Warlord. Warlords answer to a higher officer, usually the clan leader. "Clan leader" is a position held by the strongest goblin; at any time the leader may be challenged and overthrown by a more powerful Goblin.

Luckily the common goblin is just that- a nuisance that is easily scared away when confronted. Early settlers learned that just keeping a dog nearby or a lantern lit was usually enough to keep the Goblins from stealing chickens at night. *This changed in the late 5th century when Goblins began to organize themselves into clans. Suddenly there appeared Goblin war units capable of causing great harm to others. They stopped being a nuisance and became a danger. During the skirmishes of 590, the Commonwealth Guard experienced noted difficulty in suppressing Goblin raids in the southlands. After securing most of Thaermore, a large wall called the Southern Gate was built to keep the Goblins contained in Crakamir. Human settlers were evacuated from the desert lands. The Chancellor proclaimed it a victory for humans; the Goblins clans claimed it a victory for themselves. *Much was learned of the Goblin war clans at that time. The basic warrior, called the Goblin Hacker, uses a short sword or machete in a savage but effective attack. Goblin Archers have been witnessed to have impressive accuracy with short bows. And the Goblin Bombthug, a unit strapped with a keg of Bangdust, is fully prepared to sacrifice himself in the defense of the unit or a higher officer. Although most Goblins are not known to possess magickal abilities, there are reports of Goblin Shaman among the clan population. *The Goblin unit is loosely assembled and generally led by a Warlord. Warlords answer to a higher officer, usually the clan leader. "Clan leader" is a position held by the strongest goblin; at any time the leader may be challenged and overthrown by a more powerful Goblin.
Recover all four Goblin Keys and use them to enter the Goblin Citadel.

As the weeks pass, you watch the skies in the east turn dark. You hear talk in the local tavern that the Goblins continue to overtake the lands of Thaermore. The few humans who have escaped tell of the vicious Goblin raids that have brought down Blackwater and Bastion Spire. The Commonwealth Guards are powerless, the council has been disbanded and the Chancellor has disappeared.

evidence.text: This hefty tome recounts the early years of Thaermore's history in exhausting detail. Thankfully, the first chapter is an abridged timeline of events covered within the book. *CHAPTER 1 : An abridgment of historical events concerning Thaermore, eastern province of Eschalon. *--- *Year 390 - Dwarven explorer Koru Keyhammer reaches the Eastern lands known as Thaermore and reports of vast natural resources and deposits of gold, ore and gemstones. *Year 405 - The first permanent settlement called "Loneloft" is established in the mountains of western Thaermore; its founders are primarily miners and surveyors. *Year 409 - Loneloft settlers report they have encountered a peaceful race of subterranean peoples known as the Orakur. They are described as Dwarvish in build but more adapted for permanent life underground, with large eyes and little hair. *Year 419 - Skirmishes arise over control of the mines as the Orakur claim the settlers are stealing minerals from what they refer to as the "Great Underground". By Year 423 these small skirmishes had escalated into war, later to be called The Plague Wars. Dwarven settlers sign an accord absolving themselves from warring with Orakur because of a perceived kinship. Because of this accord, the Dwarven people abandon their claims and leave Thaermore; Thaermore forever becomes predominately occupied by the race of Men. *Year 425 - While mining for copper a settler named Sam of Thorabur discovers a massive gemstone that would become known as "The Crux of Ages". Because of the ongoing conflict with the Orukur the rough stone is hidden away in Bastion Spire, a stronghold which would later become the capitol of Thaermore. *Year 433 - The first governing body of Thaermore is formed. It was decreed that a lifetime Chancellor would be elected to represent the will of people. He is given the highest authority and has a council of twelve advisors, known as The Grand Scholars, serve with him. *435 - Chancellor Marr is elected as the first governor of Thaermore. Under his leadership, Thaermore establishes the Commonwealth Guard, which becomes the turning point in the war with the Orakur. *444 - The Orakur are suppressed and driven deep underground. Chancellor Marr declares victory in the war. The Orakur disappear completely and many assume the whole populous must have succumbed to disease or starvation. Dwarven Lords from outside Thaermore condemn Chancellor Marr for his unethical warfare tactics; relations between the race of Dwarves and Men are fractured. *471 - Chancellor Marr dies after 36 years of distinguished service. Chancellor Marr II, later known as "The Great One", superseded his father as Chancellor. This officially begins the golden age of expansion and prosperity for Thaermore. *509 - Chancellor Torrus I supersedes Chancellor Marr II. *537 - Chancellor Katerra I supersedes Chancellor Torrus I. *[There is an entry here that has been blackened out by ink] *590 - Goblin skirmishes arise in Crakamir. The Chancellor, unwilling to squander resources defending a wasteland, concedes Crakamir to the Goblins. Elsewhere in Thaermore, the Commonwealth Guard is successful in eliminating the Goblin threat. *627 - A devastating earthquake shakes the eastern province, tearing great rifts into the land. The Orakur, long believed to have been decimated, reappear from the great fissures. Surveyors who spot them claimed they appeared skittish and non-hostile. Elusive and rarely seen above ground, the reappearance of the Orakur is not considered a threat and they are all but forgotten. *The timeline ends here, although it looks like the following page may have been ripped from the book.

evidence.text: Gramuk leads you to a large vault just off the main vestibule in his tower room. In the vault you see huge chests filled with gold, gemstones, and priceless bars of Divine Ore. He picks up a canvas sack and begins scooping armfuls of neatly stacked coins from a table into it until the top can barely close. *"With the Crux back in our possession we now have the power to reclaim our ancient homelands. You've aided the race of Goblins, and now I make good on my offer." Gramuk lifts the hefty sack of gold and places it in your arms. "Take this gold, human. It is enough to buy passage out of Thaermore where you can retire as a wealthy lord. But heed this warning: once you leave this Citadel you will be just another human to us. Leave Thaermore and never return." *You cinch the sack of gold closed and hoist it onto your shoulder. It is heavy. Perhaps its weight is more than that of the gold alone, for you realize this sack represents the death of many humans. It represents the lands of Thaermore falling to the Goblin scourge. In time, the weight of this gold may be more than you can bear, but for now your only worry is getting out of Thaermore alive. |add_gold 83510 ; screen_fade_out ; map_port 52 ; move_player 7018 ; screen_fade_in ; areacheck|

"Sure. I don't see many travelers pass through here anymore so I'll be happy to chat for a bit. This area is called the Salted Coast because twice per year the tides rise extra high and floods most of the lowlands south of here. The soil along the shoreline is so salted that nothing grows well."\n\n"It used to be quite a nice place to live, actually. Just a few years ago I spent my days gathering salt and growing herbs to sell in Elderhollow. Then the war came and any sense of law and order disappeared. Now I spend what days I have left just defending my home from the thieves that roam this area. That's what my 'blast barrier' is for, so if any of those bastards try to get near here I'll send 'em all to their grave!"

"I don't know. All I know is that I actually kept the original letter. What I sent back to him was something I copied by hand and, well, changed a few of the instructions around." Paul smiles. "I was able to restick the wax seal on the fake letter so that it looked legitimate. There's no way the portal will ever work with the instructions I gave him!"\n\n"Look, if you really want to help me, take this original letter to someone in charge, someone who has the power to bring father Michael to justice. Don't show this to anyone in Aridell; they all think Father Michael is some sort of damned saint. They won't believe what I've told you. Take it north to Darkford and show it to the Captain who oversees operations there. He's probably the highest in authority remaining in this area of Thaermore."

evidence.text: This hefty tome recounts the early years of Thaermore's history in exhausting detail. Thankfully, the first chapter is an abridged timeline of events covered within the book. *CHAPTER 1 : An abridgment of historical events concerning Thaermore, eastern province of Eschalon. *--- *Year 390 - Dwarven explorer Koru Keyhammer reaches the Eastern lands known as Thaermore and reports of vast natural resources and deposits of gold, ore and gemstones. *Year 405 - The first permanent settlement called "Loneloft" is established in the mountains of western Thaermore; its founders are primarily miners and surveyors. *Year 409 - Loneloft settlers report they have encountered a peaceful race of subterranean peoples known as the Orakur. They are described as Dwarvish in build but more adapted for permanent life underground, with large eyes and little hair. *Year 419 - Skirmishes arise over control of the mines as the Orakur claim the settlers are stealing minerals from what they refer to as the "Great Underground". By Year 423 these small skirmishes had escalated into war, later to be called The Plague Wars. Dwarven settlers sign an accord absolving themselves from warring with Orakur because of a perceived kinship. Because of this accord, the Dwarven people abandon their claims and leave Thaermore; Thaermore forever becomes predominately occupied by the race of Men. *Year 425 - While mining for copper a settler named Sam of Thorabur discovers a massive gemstone that would become known as "The Crux of Ages". Because of the ongoing conflict with the Orukur the rough stone is hidden away in Bastion Spire, a stronghold which would later become the capitol of Thaermore. *Year 433 - The first governing body of Thaermore is formed. It was decreed that a lifetime Chancellor would be elected to represent the will of people. He is given the highest authority and has a council of twelve advisors, known as The Grand Scholars, serve with him. *435 - Chancellor Marr is elected as the first governor of Thaermore. Under his leadership, Thaermore establishes the Commonwealth Guard, which becomes the turning point in the war with the Orakur. *444 - The Orakur are suppressed and driven deep underground. Chancellor Marr declares victory in the war. The Orakur disappear completely and many assume the whole populous must have succumbed to disease or starvation. Dwarven Lords from outside Thaermore condemn Chancellor Marr for his unethical warfare tactics; relations between the race of Dwarves and Men are fractured. *471 - Chancellor Marr dies after 36 years of distinguished service. Chancellor Marr II, later known as "The Great One", superseded his father as Chancellor. This officially begins the golden age of expansion and prosperity for Thaermore. *509 - Chancellor Torrus I supersedes Chancellor Marr II. *537 - Chancellor Katerra I supersedes Chancellor Torrus I. *[There is an entry here that has been blackened out by ink] *590 - Goblin skirmishes arise in Crakamir. The Chancellor, unwilling to squander resources defending a wasteland, concedes Crakamir to the Goblins. Elsewhere in Thaermore, the Commonwealth Guard is successful in eliminating the Goblin threat. *627 - A devastating earthquake shakes the eastern province, tearing great rifts into the land. The Orakur, long believed to have been decimated, reappear from the great fissures. Surveyors who spot them claimed they appeared skittish and non-hostile. Elusive and rarely seen above ground, the reappearance of the Orakur is not considered a threat and they are all but forgotten. *The timeline ends here, although it looks like the following page may have been ripped from the book.

evidence.text: $, *Well done! If you are reading this then you have completed a difficult series of tasks designed to ensure your safety. Although enough time has passed for you to have firmly solidified your new identity, the danger surrounding your previous identity is not completely eliminated. Still, it should be a bit safer now to fill you in on some of the mystery surrounding your past. *First, you undoubtedly see the large gemstone in the box along with this note. Yes, this is the legendary "Crux of Ages" that I'm sure you have heard about. Take it with you and keep it close. It will protect you, but if you show it to anyone it will certainly lead to your death. *Now for how this came into your possession: you found it while scavenging a goblin battlefield looking for valuables. I cannot describe the details of the actual discovery to you now because if it were to trigger memories of the event, your life would be in certain danger. Let me explain: *A powerful Goblin Shaman named Gramuk is using a technique called "Temporal Linking" to locate the person who recovered the Crux. You see, every action you do is etched in your mind as a memory, forever linked to a lifetime of previously accumulated memories. Thus, the event of you finding the Crux was linked to all the memories associated with your prior identity. Scryers who perform Temporal Linking can use these linked memories to identify and locate people by focusing in on specific events. Erasing your identity and all associated memories means Gramuk is unable to connect the event of recovering the gemstone back to you. Even after taking possession of the Crux now, the lack of chronological memories linking you to the gem means it will be many weeks before Gramuk will be able to scry enough information to locate you. *So have you figured out who I am yet? Certainly you must have speculated by now that I am you. Yes, you set this all up to protect yourself- you wrote these notes and devised this scheme to destroy your memory and build a new identity. *Now this is where things get complicated and I will do my best to help you understand what is happening. First, you were not alone when you found the Crux: your brother was with you and shared in the recovery and concealment of the gemstone. He had planned to erase his memory along with you, but he was located and captured by the Goblins before he was able to complete the task. The only chance you had of helping him was to follow through with the plan and erase your own memory first. Now that you've accomplished this, you must locate and help your brother. The Goblins will keep him alive as long as they believe they can extract information from him, but the torture he must be enduring is unthinkable. Days ago, just before you erased your memory, you heard from a Ranger passing through Tanglewood that he may have been taken to the abandoned city Vela, which is now a goblin outpost. *There are many more questions surrounding this war, such as the Chancellor believing that the Orakur have stolen the gem even though evidence strongly points to the Goblins. This evidence, along with the Chancellor's incongruous war plan to abandon security across Thaermore, substantiates the theory that Gramuk is somehow influencing the Chancellor. While you may believe none of this information concerns you, it does, because eventually the Crux will be tracked back to you; eventually your brother will be killed when he is of no more use to the Goblins; and eventually all of Thaermore will fall to the spreading Goblin insurgence. Like it or not, you have become a significant factor in this war. *If you fled now, I wouldn't blame you. You could toss the gem into a river, leave your brother whom you have no memories of to his fate and start a new life somewhere else. However, I know you are stronger person than that. Please, locate and help your brother. He is the only family you have.

evidence.text: $, *You don't know who I am, but I know who you are. I'm sure you are very confused right now, but you must gather yourself quickly. I've hidden a few basic supplies for you- they are out back near the well. Hopefully you'll remember the secret spot. You need to find a man named Maddock in the village of Aridell, which is just a short walk northeast of here. $, *If you are reading this then you have made it safely to Aridell and found Maddock. I could not risk leaving this document with you due to the sensitivity of the information I am about to disclose. I was unsure how long you'd be unconscious and I couldn't risk having this document end up in the wrong hands. Maddock is a simple man who has lived in this village most of his life and I knew he'd be a trustworthy caretaker of this parcel I left for you. Use the gold to buy supplies for yourself- whatever you need to secure your safety and well being. I wish I could have left you more, but it was all I had. *I'm sure you are wondering who I am. My identity will be revealed in time, but for now you should simply trust me. Whether you decide to or not is your choice. *Now, about yourself: you are part of something very big- an event that has affected this entire region. For your safety you were placed into hiding and your memory was erased with a special serum. The name you think you remember, $, was imprinted in your mind. I will not reveal your true name here because of the danger it would bring you, so you should continue to live by the name $. It would be wise for you to not draw attention to yourself by asking too many questions about your past. *Your true identity can be revealed to you but only if you are willing to accept the risk that accompanies it. You must decide for yourself whether to seek the truth or simply become "$" and settle into this new life. If you choose the path of truth it will be a hard and dangerous journey. *And so, if the truth is what you seek, you need to start by retrieving an amulet that belongs to you. Before your memory was taken, you requested that I secure a special amulet for you. I did so by slipping it into the coffin of a recently deceased aristocrat named "Adler Keldam". He is interred in a vault at Eversleep Cemetery in the North Parish region. I knew his casket would be a secure place to hide your amulet; the problem now is retrieving it. The door to the crypt is locked tight. Smashing the door down or picking the lock might be an option, but it may be easiest to just get the key. The cemetery director, Leurik, lives a bit north of Aridell and he has the key. I am confident that you could figure out a way to get it from him. *Once you retrieve your amulet from the crypt, take it to a woman named Lilith who lives in Tangletree Forest. Look for her house in the "heart of the woods". She will tell you what she knows of this amulet and set you on the right path. *Finally, you must use this time to rebuild your strength, stamina and knowledge. You were once very proficient in many skills, which the serum has caused you to forget. Only through experience and practice will you be able to reacquire these Skills you have lost. It is the only way you'll be safe. *:E:

evidence.text: "Grimmhold is an old fortress which lies just a short walk west of here. It once served as a gateway between this area and western Thaermore, cutting a swath through the thickest part of Tangletree Forest. It also bridges the Eastern Gap, a huge rift cut into the ground that lies in the center of the forest." \n\n"After the conflict began, the Commonwealth Guards who held Grimmhold were called to service by the Chancellor. Soon after their departure, Goblins overran and took control of the fortress. It fell, just like Elderhollow southwest of here."

"Yes! Vile creatures, those Goblins are. In the past they've posed little threat to us humans, but with our resources spread thin and our attention focused on the conflict with the Orakur, they've taken advantage of the situation and now run amok. In my opinion their taking of Grimmhold is just the start. If the Chancellor doesn't change his war plan they are going to become a bigger threat than the Orakur!"\n\nAbygale pauses and takes a deep breath, aware that she has upset herself. "Grimmhold is now unsafe and probably not even passable. If you absolutely must travel west, you should take the northern pass. Unfortunately, this is a much longer journey and probably just as dangerous- but I guess it's safer than trying to go around Tangletree Forest to the south. The southern route is plagued with bandits."
